parts.text:
7
An astronaut on the Moon, where there is no air resistance, throws a ball. The ball’s initial velocity
has a vertical component of 8.00 m s–1 and a horizontal component of 4.00 m s–1, as shown.
initial velocity
path of ball
8.00 m s–1
4.00 m s–1
The acceleration of free fall on the Moon is 1.62 m s–2.
What will be the speed of the ball 9.00 s after being thrown?
A
6.6 m s–1
B
7.7 m s–1
C
10.6 m s–1
D
14.6 m s–1

hints: Notice the motion splits: horizontal velocity stays at $4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ because there is no air resistance, while vertical velocity changes under Moon gravity.
Use $v_y = u_y - gt$ with $u_y = 8.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $g = 1.62\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $t = 9.00\text{ s}$ - check whether the sign shows the ball is now falling.
Combine the two perpendicular components at $9.00\text{ s}$ with speed $= \sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2}$, not by adding them directly.
walkthrough: Horizontal component is unchanged with no air resistance, so $v_x = 4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $9.00\text{ s}$.
Vertical motion has constant downward acceleration $g = 1.62\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Take upward as positive: $v_y = u_y - gt$.
Substitute $v_y = 8.00 - (1.62)(9.00) = 8.00 - 14.58 = -6.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The negative sign means the ball is moving downward, past the top of its path.
Speed is the magnitude of the resultant velocity: $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(4.00)^2 + (-6.58)^2}$.
Calculate $v = \sqrt{16.0 + 43.30} = \sqrt{59.30} \approx 7.7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with units of speed. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is the magnitude of the vertical component only, $|v_y| \approx 6.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and it omits the $4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ horizontal component.

B.explanation: This is $\sqrt{(4.00)^2+(-6.58)^2} \approx 7.7\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the resultant of the unchanged horizontal velocity and the vertical velocity after $9.00\text{ s}$.

C.explanation: This is about $14.58-4.00 = 10.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which incorrectly subtracts the horizontal speed from the vertical change $gt$ instead of combining perpendicular components with Pythagoras.

D.explanation: This is $gt = 1.62 \times 9.00 = 14.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the change in vertical velocity only, ignoring the $8.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ initial upward velocity and the horizontal motion.
